messages.subject: String Counting Question
parts:
Hi, I'm having trouble wrapping my head around how to count strings in R.  I have a data.table (see sample data below) with information about different hospitalizations, including diagnosis codes (characters).  I also have a character vector of the diagnosis codes related to organ dysfunction.  I'd like to know: for each hospitalization, how many organ dysfunctions occurred during the hospitalization?  

SAMPLE DATA:

print(hospitalization)
hospitalization_no, diagnosis1, diagnosis2, LOS, diagnosis3, 
100567, 0700, 51881, 19, 0052
100568, 9847, 0300, 4, 4011
100569, 3187, 3481, 2, 2939

#note: LOS is an integer 

organ_dysfunction = c("5185", "51881", "51882", "51884", "51885", "78609", "7991", "0967", "09671", "09672", "4275", "4580", "4582", "4588", "4589", "78550", "75851", "75852", "75859", "7963", "580", "5804", "5800", "58081", "58089", "5809", "584", "5845", "5846", "5847", "5848", "5849", "570", "5722", "5733", "2866", "2869", "2873", "2874", "2875", "2762", "2930", "2931", "2939", "3481", "3483", "34831", "34839", "78001", "78009", "99592")


My ideal output would be:
hospitalization_no, diagnosis1, diagnosis2, LOS, diagnosis3, organ_dysfunction
100567, 0700, 51881, 19, 0052, 1
100568, 9847, 0300, 4, 4011, 0
100569, 3187, 3481, 2, 2939, 2


This would also be a great output:
Number of Organ Dysfunctions, Number of Cases
One, 30000
Two, 20000
Three, 10000
Four+, 2000
 
I thought about using the reshape package, but I'm reading that it's not great with strings.  stringr also came to mind, but I'm unsure how to get to it work with a data.table.  Many. many thanks in advance.

Here I’m using dplyr syntax to do this. dplyr works well on data.tables. You could do this in data.table’s own syntax but I’m screwing it up trying that. dplyr’s syntax is a little more verbose but rather clear.

library(data.table)
library(dplyr)

# rebuilding the example data
# Next time you can make sure we have the same data by pasting the results of
# dput(hospitalization[1:3,]) into your email
hospitalization = as.data.frame(rbind(c(100567, 0700, 51881, 19, 0052),
c(100568, 9847, 0300, 4, 4011),
c(100569, 3187, 3481, 2, 2939)))
names(hospitalization) = c("hospitalization_no", "diagnosis1", "diagnosis2", "LOS", "diagnosis3")

hospitalization$diagnosis1 = as.character(hospitalization$diagnosis1)
hospitalization$diagnosis2 = as.character(hospitalization$diagnosis2)
hospitalization$diagnosis3 = as.character(hospitalization$diagnosis3)
organ_dysfunction = c("5185", "51881", "51882", "51884", "51885", "78609", "7991", "0967", "09671", "09672", "4275", "4580", "4582", "4588", "4589", "78550", "75851", "75852", "75859", "7963", "580", "5804", "5800", "58081", "58089", "5809", "584", "5845", "5846", "5847", "5848", "5849", "570", "5722", "5733", "2866", "2869", "2873", "2874", "2875", "2762", "2930", "2931", "2939", "3481", "3483", "34831", "34839", "78001", "78009", "99592")

hospitalization = data.table(hospitalization)

##
# OK, now the operations only take a few lines:

#Make a column called "organ function" which is the sum of 3 logical tests
# Logical values are coerced to 0 and 1, so you get the count across the diagnoses
hospitalization = hospitalization %>%
  mutate(organ_function = diagnosis1 %in% organ_dysfunction + diagnosis2 %in% organ_dysfunction +diagnosis3 %in% organ_dysfunction)

# Summarize, counting all the rows in subsets divided up
# by the number of dysfunction counts.  Note that n() gives row count.
dysfunction_counts = hospitalization %>%
  group_by(organ_function) %>%
  summarize(no_cases = n())
​
